## What

A federated write goes through **two** ordering decisions, and they must agree:

1. **The merge winners-fold** (`read-merge.ts` `mergeAdmittedLogs`, whose
   `beatsStored` comparator — defined in `read-merge.ts` as a hand-mirror of
   `projection.ts`'s `lwwPick` — decides winners) — since P-010 this
   orders by the op's **HLC** when
   both ops carry one, else falls back to wall-clock `ts`.
2. **The PG projection LWW guard** (`harness-features.ts` etc.) — the
   `INSERT … ON CONFLICT … WHERE stored.fed_ts IS NULL OR EXCLUDED.fed_ts >=
   stored.fed_ts` clause — orders by **`fed_ts`**.

If these two disagree under same-key contention, the system **silently
diverges**: the merge picks op X as the winner and hands it to `apply`, but the
PG guard rejects X (its `fed_ts` lost) → no write → the cell keeps its own
value. Each cell keeps its own → the two cells "converge" (no more ops to
drain, `fixedPoint=true`) to **different** values. The tripwire was
`split-brain-mug.integration.test.ts` (both Mugs steer opposite orders;
cell A ended with a mix, cell B with all-its-own).

## Why they disagreed

- **`fed_ts`** is stamped at the **local write** (migration 214
  `stamp_local_federated_write`, `clock_timestamp()`).
- **HLC** was stamped at **DRAIN** (`stampOpHlc` in `hlc-stamp.ts` called from
  `boot.ts`'s `handle.append`, using a bare `clock.now()` = wall-clock-at-drain).

Drain happens later than — and in a different order than — the writes (the CDC
outbox drains in batches, concurrently across cells), so the HLC ordered ops by
**drain-interleave** while `fed_ts` ordered them by **write time**. An op could
win the HLC fold but lose the `fed_ts` guard.

## Fix

Seed the HLC's physical component from the op's **own recorded write-time `ts`**
(the outbox row's capture `ts`, ≈ `fed_ts`), not the wall clock at stamp time:

```ts
// hlc-stamp.ts
export function stampOpHlc(op, clock = processHlc()) {
  if (op.hlc) return op;
  return { ...op, hlc: encodeHlc(clock.now(op.ts)) }; // was clock.now()
}
```

`HlcClock.send(physicalNow)` is built for exactly this ("seed from an event's
own recorded ms") and stays monotone via `bumpCount` when `ts` is in the past,
so causality (the RECV-seam `observeRemoteHlc` advance) is preserved. The
merge's HLC order matches the PG guard's `fed_ts` order → no silent rejection
**FOR THE DRAIN-INTERLEAVE CASE**.

> ⚠️ **This 2026-06-14 patch was INCOMPLETE (it closed only the drain-interleave
> trigger) and was later REOPENED then fully RESOLVED — see "## REOPENED (D-001)"
> and "## RESOLVED" below.** Seeding the HLC from `op.ts` only guarantees
> `HLC.physical ≥ op.ts` for the SAME op. It does NOT make the HLC ORDER of two
> CONCURRENT ops match their `fed_ts` order, because the RECV-seam advance this
> patch DELIBERATELY PRESERVES raises a peer's clock ABOVE a later write's `ts`
> (`send(ts)` returns `max(clock.physical, ts)`). The split-brain was still
> reachable until the D-001 ordering-key fix shipped.

## Gotchas when reproducing in a rig

`composition-rig.ts` simulates **two swarms in ONE process**. Real swarms are
separate processes with **independent** HLC clocks, but the rig shared the
process-global `processHlc()` singleton — so the two cells' concurrent drains
raced the same counter and decided cross-swarm LWW by drain-interleave. Give
each cell its **own** `HlcClock` (gated `hlcClock` seams on `boot.ts`
`BootHarnessOpts`, `projection.ts` `ApplyOpOpts`, `hlc-stamp.ts`; default
`processHlc()` so production is unchanged). See
[[substrate-hlc-and-capture-coverage]] and
[[two-federation-paths-cannot-share-one-fed-ts]].

## Smell test

If two federated cells end a converge() with DIFFERENT values for the same key
(and `fixedPoint=true`), suspect an ordering-key mismatch between the merge fold
and a projection's PG LWW guard — they must use the SAME key.

## REOPENED (D-001, 2026-06-19, shared-pot-release-testing Brief D)

The 2026-06-14 fix closed the **drain-interleave** trigger but NOT the root
cause: the merge fold orders by **HLC** and the PG guard orders by **fed_ts =
op.ts**, and these are still two different clocks. Seeding HLC from `op.ts` makes
`HLC.physical ≥ op.ts` for one op, but the RECV seam (`observeRemoteHlc`, kept on
purpose) advances a peer's `HlcClock` ABOVE a later write's `ts`. Then:

- Winner **W**: its author observed a remote op at HLC.physical = 9000 (recv
  advance), then wrote KEY at wall `ts = 1000` → HLC `(9000,·)`, **fed_ts 1000**.
- Loser **L**: a fresh-clock peer wrote KEY at `ts = 5000` → HLC `(5000,0)`,
  **fed_ts 5000**.

`lwwPick`/`beatsStored` pick W (higher HLC); the PG guard prefers L (higher
fed_ts). The merge SUPPRESSES the HLC-loser once the HLC-winner is the standing
winner, and the PG guard REJECTS the HLC-winner when its fed_ts lost — so the two
authors materialise different rows and never reconcile:

- W's author folds W first → PG = W; L arrives, beatsStored(L,W)=false → suppressed.
- L's author folds L first → PG = L; W arrives, handed to apply → `WHERE
  EXCLUDED.fed_ts(1000) >= stored.fed_ts(5000)` is FALSE → rejected → PG stays L.

**Reachability:** HLC.physical is monotone and propagates the GLOBAL-max wall-ts
seen anywhere (recv takes `max`). A single forward clock excursion on ANY peer
(NTP overshoot, fast VM, manual set) raises the HLC floor for everyone
permanently; thereafter any concurrent same-key writes whose wall-`ts` order
differs across peers can diverge. The window self-heals only once every peer's
wall clock advances past the floor.

**Why the green suite missed it (still):** `split-brain-mug` and the
composition rig share one wall clock (`physical: () => this.now()`), so they
can't construct recv-advance + skew. `three-peer-partition-rejoin` asserts
convergence at the read-merge layer with a TEST-LOCAL ts-only LWW and an injected
sink — it exercises neither the HLC fold nor the PG guard, the two layers whose
disagreement IS the bug.

**Repro (current `staging`):**
`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/__tests__/lww-hlc-fedts-divergence.test.ts`
(fast, real merge + faithful guard), its `.integration.test.ts` twin (real PG
projection), and the seeded `convergence-fuzz.test.ts` (monotone sweep GREEN,
skew sweep finds it).

## RESOLVED (D-001 fix shipped)

The one-ordering-key-of-record fix landed. Migration
`314-d001-hlc-ordering-key.sql` adds a **`fed_hlc`** column to the mutable LWW
tables, and the projection PG guards now order by it (the HLC), with `fed_ts`
kept only as a fallback when a row predates the column — so the merge fold and
the PG guard finally use the SAME key. The HLC-winner can no longer be silently
rejected by a `fed_ts`-loser guard, so concurrent same-key writes converge to one
value across cells even under recv-advance skew. The seeded `convergence-fuzz`
suite asserts it: `S0 (D-001) FIXED: the skew sweep fully converges under the
shipped fed_hlc guard`
(`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/__tests__/convergence-fuzz.test.ts`).
The original `lww-hlc-fedts-divergence.test.ts` repro is now the regression
tripwire.

## FURTHER REFINED (EI-1698 + WI-1672 — mig 458/459/466)

D-001 (above) made the merge fold and the PG guard order by the SAME field
(`fed_hlc`, falling back to `fed_ts`), but two more divergence modes surfaced
after it shipped — both closed by refining the SQL comparator, not by
reopening the ordering-key question:

- **EI-1698 (transitivity, migration `458-fed-order-key-transitivity-fix.sql`):**
  the original guard's rule — "if BOTH sides carry an HLC compare HLC, else
  compare bare `ts`" — is **non-transitive** when HLC presence is mixed (a
  rolling-upgrade / pre-P-010-history scenario): three ops `X` (hlc+ts), `Y`
  (ts-only), `Z` (hlc+ts) can cycle `X>Z, Z>Y, Y>X`, so two peers applying the
  same ops in a different delivery order pick different winners. The fix gives
  every op **one comparable key** — its real `hlc` when present, else a
  *derived* `encodeHlc({ms: ts ?? 0, count: 0})` — and compares that single
  derived key for every pair. `lwwPick` (`projection.ts`) already folded this
  in-process; migration 458 adds the SQL mirror, `harness_shared.fed_order_key(hlc,
  ts)`, so every writer's `ON CONFLICT` / `DELETE` guard (`fed_order_key(EXCLUDED…)
  >= fed_order_key(stored…)`) compares in the exact same order space as the fold
  and can no longer reject what the fold picked.
- **WI-1672 (exact-tie split-brain, migrations `459-hlc-node-id-total-order.sql` +
  `466-hlc-node-id-strong-entropy.sql`):** `hlc_recv`/`observeRemoteHlc` ratchet
  every peer's clock to the max wall-ms ever witnessed pot-wide, so after any
  transient fast-clock episode all peers advance by logical counter only, in
  near-lockstep — two peers then routinely mint an **identical** `fed_hlc` for
  concurrent writes to the same key, and the guard's tie-ACCEPTING `>=` lets the
  incoming remote op overwrite the local row on BOTH sides — a stable swap, not a
  crash, so it's easy to miss. The fix makes the ordering key **total by
  construction**: every `Hlc` now carries an optional `node` identity segment
  (`libs/generic/locks-core/src/hlc.ts`, `HLC_NODE_LEN = 16` lowercase-hex),
  `compareHlc`/`encodeHlc` break `(ms, count)` ties on it, and `HlcClock` stamps
  its own node onto every value it mints — so a genuine full tie can only be the
  *same* stamp replayed (where tie-accept is correct and idempotent). Migration
  459 seeds each device's `hlc_clock.node_id` from SQL `random()`; migration 466
  found that formula (`md5(random()::text || clock_timestamp()::text ||
  pg_backend_pid()::text)`) can collide across two backends started in close
  succession on the same PG server (observed in CI), and reseeds from
  pgcrypto's `gen_random_bytes()` instead — a decorrelated source engineered for
  exactly that "many callers, narrow time window" shape. No comparator or format
  change: a node-less legacy stamp is a strict string-prefix of any node-carrying
  sibling with the same `(ms, count)`, so it loses the tie identically on every
  peer/collation.

Both fixes are additive to D-001's ordering key (`fed_hlc`/`fed_order_key`),
not a new one — they make its *comparator* transitive and its *ties* total,
closing the two windows a same-key-contention smell test should now also
cover: (a) mixed HLC-presence cycling across 3+ peers, (b) two peers minting
the exact same `fed_hlc`.

## FURTHER REFINED (WI-2923/WI-2933 — mig 504, `fed_apply_wins`)

WI-1672 (above) made a genuine full HLC *tie* total by construction (a node
segment breaks `(ms, count)` ties), but that only covers two peers minting the
literal **same** `fed_hlc`. It does NOT cover two peers minting **different**
`fed_hlc`s that still collapse to an **equal `fed_order_key`** — e.g. two
cells independently completing the SAME item in the same clock tick with
distinct per-writer HLCs. Before WI-2923, the PG apply-guard's `WHERE
fed_order_key(EXCLUDED…) >= fed_order_key(stored…)` applied
**UNCONDITIONALLY** on such a key tie: each cell's own write beats-or-ties its
own stored row (`>=` is reflexive), so **both** cells apply the **other's**
value on heal — a stable value SWAP, not a rejection, so it slips past the
`fixedPoint=true`-with-divergent-values smell test silently (no rejected op to
notice; composition-chaos P-002, `F-003 winner a/b swap`).

The fix (migration `504-fed-apply-writer-tiebreak.sql`) replaces the bare
`>=` with a SQL function, **`harness_shared.fed_apply_wins(...)`**, that
resolves an equal-key tie deterministically and *symmetrically* across every
replica:

1. Strictly newer/older `fed_order_key` → apply/reject as before.
2. **Equal key, both writers known and different** → the higher
   `author_pubkey` wins on every replica (value-independent, mirrors
   `beatsStored`'s `sourceLogKeyHex` total-order tiebreak).
3. **Otherwise** (a writer unknown — local rows are `author_pubkey NULL` by
   design, mig 214 — or the same writer) → the higher **content digest**
   wins. The digest is computed SYMMETRICALLY over content columns only
   (never `fed_ts`/`fed_hlc`/`origin`/`author_pubkey`/bookkeeping), so cell A
   comparing `digest(B) vs digest(A)` and cell B comparing `digest(A) vs
   digest(B)` settle on the SAME content in one exchange; equal digests mean
   identical content, so applying is an idempotent no-op.

`fed_apply_wins` was rolled out to every LWW projection's apply-guard, not
just `harness-features.ts`: `engineer-issues.ts`, `fleet-leader-leases.ts`
(WI-2923), then `coord-message.ts`, `contributors.ts`, and
`fleet-directory.ts` (WI-2933, extending the same function to more
projections). Regression coverage:
`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/hyperbee/projections/__tests__/fed-ts-lww-guard.integration.test.ts`
(same-writer equal-key falls to the digest tiebreak) and
`fleet-leader-leases.test.ts` (asserts the guard SQL calls `fed_apply_wins`).

⚠️ **This tie-break lives in the PG apply-guard only** — `read-merge.ts`'s
in-process fold (`beatsStored`) still orders an equal-`fed_order_key`
(same-`ts`) tie by `sourceLogKeyHex` alone, not by writer-pubkey-then-digest.
The two layers' tie-break rules are therefore not byte-identical; they were
not observed to diverge in practice (the fold's `sourceLogKeyHex` total order
already prevents the fold itself from flip-flopping), but a future smell-test
pass should treat "the merge fold and the PG guard use a different equal-key
tiebreak" as the same class of risk this whole doc is about.

## FURTHER REFINED (EI-8210 — mig 517 regressed, mig 528 restores, `fed_hlc` stamping)

D-001 (above) made `stamp_local_federated_write()`'s INSERT branch stamp
**both** `fed_ts` AND `fed_hlc` on a local write, so the ordering key the fold
and the PG guard both read is always populated. Migration **517**
(`517-fix-stamp-local-federated-write-mask.sql`, WI-183/WI-2845/WI-2853) fixed
an UNRELATED bug in the SAME trigger function — a same-op double-apply
re-stamping `work_items.updated_ts` on every replay and false-positiving a
"real content change", flipping an already-`origin='remote'` row back to
`'local'` — but the `CREATE OR REPLACE` that shipped that fix rewrote the whole
function body from an older copy and **silently dropped the `fed_hlc :=
harness_shared.hlc_now()` stamp on the local-INSERT branch**, regressing it
back to fed_ts-only (the pre-D-001 shape). A local `INSERT` after mig 517
landed stamped `fed_ts` but left `fed_hlc` **NULL**.

Migration 477's `capture_hive_members_outbox` (a stamp-regime table, unlike
`work_items`) threads a captured row's `fed_ts`/`fed_hlc` straight into the
outbox op's `ts`/`hlc`; with `fed_hlc` NULL, every `hive_members` admission/
revocation capture fell back to the drain clock instead of the author's real
ordering key — reopening the exact drain-interleave divergence class from the
top of this doc (the "## Fix" section, migration 314/490), just on a
different table.

Migration **528** (`528-restore-fed-hlc-insert-stamp.sql`) restores the
`fed_hlc` stamp on the local-INSERT branch (and adds the missing
`hlc_recv()` causal-advance call on a remote INSERT that carries an HLC,
matching the UPDATE branch's existing recv-advance) while KEEPING mig 517's
`work_items`-only `updated_ts`/`ts` double-apply mask intact — the two fixes
are orthogonal (one is which columns count as "content changed", the other is
which columns get stamped on a genuine local write) and mig 528 is careful not
to re-regress the other.

**Smell-test addendum:** a `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` on this trigger is a
recurring risk point — mig 517 proves a *well-intentioned, narrowly-scoped*
fix to one branch can silently regress a DIFFERENT branch's D-001 stamping if
the replacement body isn't diffed against the full prior function. Any future
edit to `stamp_local_federated_write()` should diff against the CURRENT
`CREATE OR REPLACE` (not an older migration) and confirm both branches still
stamp `fed_hlc`, not just `fed_ts`.
